results.title: Vokal: A collaboration space for 10x teammates with their Al agents | Product Hunt
results.content:
Vokal gives humans and agents one shared workspace so the team can align the goal, assign the right agent, watch the work, review in context, and save useful outputs for the next run.

Here’s how it works:

1. Bring teammates and agents into one shared workspace.
2. Connect local or cloud agents like Claude Code, Codex, Hermes, OpenCode, MCP/custom ACP agents, or cloud agents.
3. Give each agent a name, role, owner, permissions, app access, and memory scope.
4. Run work in channels with tasks, docs, routines, Memory, and Knowledge Base attached.
5. Nudge the work in context and save useful outputs so the next teammate or agent can start from what the team already learned.

Why startups use Vokal: [...] Reviews

Most Informative

•1 review

#### What's great

Vokal makes AI agent work feel much more collaborative and organized. Instead of having context, tasks, and outputs scattered across private chats or separate tools, everything happens in a shared real-time workspace.

What I like most is that humans and agents can coordinate before the final output is delivered. It makes the work easier to review, easier to follow, and easier to reuse later.

#### vs Alternatives

SlackSlackGitHubGitHubChatGPT by OpenAIChatGPT by OpenAI

I’ve used a mix of AI chat tools, team docs, Slack, GitHub, and task trackers to coordinate work with AI. [...] Congrats on the launch!

Report

Vamshi Reddy

The human-to-agent handoff is where most teams are still flying blind. At Tuple, when we started running AI agents across client campaigns, the breakdown wasn't the agents — it was that no one could see what they'd done or what needed human review before going out. We built a manual paper trail for that. Treating agents as first-class teammates with permissions, ownership, and an event log is exactly the right architecture. Teams that nail this in the next 18 months will have a real operational edge.

Report

Zhen Han

Vokal

Maker

@thekrew Exactly. The failure mode isn’t usually that the agent did nothing, it’s invisible work. Who asked? What context was used? What changed? What still needs review before it ships?

A desktop app for Git branches and GitHub pull requests. Comment on any line, publish when you're ready, and add an AI reviewer with your own model, or none. Since AI started writing so much of our code, reviewing it all has become the hardest part of my job. So I built Review: a desktop app for reviewing pull requests, where you can set up a team of AI reviewers from different providers to take the first pass. - Opens your local Git branches and GitHub pull requests in one window. - Keeps your comments on your machine until you publish them to GitHub as a review. **What's different about the AI part**: it checks every change against a fixed set of rules (bugs, security, error handling, tests and more), and it shows which rules it actually checked, not just what it found. If a request fails, you can retry only the rules it missed. One heads-up: the installers aren't signed yet, so your system will ask once the first time you open it.
